solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Famous crooner keeps awkward person in tears

indicators.note: a singer who keeps something holds it within, so one name goes round the other word

parts.note: Bing Crosby, the celebrated crooner
a lubber is a clumsy, ungainly fellow, as in landlubber

explanation.surface: A celebrity singer has some clumsy hanger-on reduced to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' is the containment signal; the crooner is Bing Crosby, and a lubber is an old word for a clumsy oaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Sobbing noisily is the state of someone in floods of tears, so the phrase and the verb form match.

clue.text: Fleeing Welsh city, men strike

indicators.note: fleeing means the soldiers leave, so their letters are removed from the city

parts.note: Bangor is a cathedral city in north Wales
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Workers walk out of a Welsh city and go on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleeing' takes OR from BANGOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To bang something is to hit it hard, so it is a synonym for strike.

clue.text: Do without fine ointment

indicators.note: without means the following letter is taken away

parts.note: a do is a party or social event, a function
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Managing without some quality ointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes F from FUNCTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Unction is an old word for a soothing oil or salve rubbed on the skin.

clue.text: Remove access to facilities in high-rise housing

parts.note: to block off a place is to stop anyone getting in
lats is informal, chiefly military slang for latrines, i.e. toilet facilities

explanation.surface: Closing off the lavatories in a tower block.
explanation.walkthrough: LATS is short for latrines, the toilet facilities.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall building divided into many apartments is a classic form of high-rise housing.

clue.text: Comfort a son in note — definitely!

indicators.note: in places the pieces in a row after the note, between it and the next word

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
sure means definitely, as in 'sure, I will'

explanation.surface: Someone consoling a boy with a written note, emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' here just slots 'a son' into the run after the sol-fa note, before 'definitely'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassure someone is to put their mind at rest, to soothe their worries.

clue.text: Reportedly kissed that girl in 'ackney? It's very tasteful

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are heard spoken, not written

parts.note: necked 'er: kissed (necked) her, with the h dropped in Cockney fashion, as in 'ackney for Hackney

explanation.surface: A cockney's tale of a kiss in Hackney, praised as delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: To neck is informal for kissing passionately; Hackney is in East London, where Cockney speech drops the initial h.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink of the gods in Greek myth, and so anything deliciously flavoured.

clue.text: Lacking energy, put on party

indicators.note: lacking says the following letter is missing from the word for put on

parts.note: to stage a play is to put it on
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone too tired to throw a party they had planned to host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking' drops an E from STAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag (do) is a men-only party held for a groom before his wedding.

clue.text: Water creature avoiding soft ground

indicators.note: avoiding means the following letter is kept out of the word

parts.note: a terrapin is a freshwater turtle
p, piano, is the musical notation for soft

explanation.surface: An aquatic animal steering clear of boggy land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' takes P from TERRAPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land considered for its physical features, so ground.

clue.text: Dancer's sleep is something sweet

parts.note: Ginger Rogers, Fred Astaire's dance partner, with the possessive s
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A ballet dancer's rest is something lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp ginger-flavoured biscuit, a sweet treat.

clue.text: Black magic may concern criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Sorcery could be a worry for a lawbreaker, or something a crook may meddle with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges MAY CONCERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Necromancy is sorcery that claims to summon the dead, the classic dark art.

clue.text: Food with short tradename

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: a brand is the trade name under which goods are sold

explanation.surface: A foodstuff sold under a brief brand name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' takes the final D from BRAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran is the husk of cereal grain, eaten as a breakfast food for fibre.

clue.text: Reserve supports Hertfordshire town

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire, a county north of London

explanation.surface: A reserve fund propping up a small town in the Home Counties.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-string player is a substitute or backup, kept in reserve.

clue.text: Noise from animal fair ringing round most of pub

indicators.note: ringing round means encircling, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: fair in the sense of so-so, satisfactory, is OK

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A noise at a country fair where animals are penned around a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like a country show but means satisfactory; 'most of' docks the pub word and 'ringing round' wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: The grunting sound a pig makes is conventionally written this way.

clue.text: Draw colleague, not British

indicators.note: not says the following letter is left out of the word for colleague

parts.note: a stablemate is a fellow member of the same organisation or team

explanation.surface: An instruction to sketch a co-worker who happens to be foreign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes B from STABLEMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a position where no legal move exists ends the game as a draw.

clue.text: These shows that I'm playing could be Test Match Special

indicators.note: playing suggests things being played about with, so the letters are shuffled together

explanation.surface: A commentator musing that these programmes might be Test Match Special.
explanation.walkthrough: 'These' stands for the answer: its letters plus THAT I'M, mixed by 'playing', give TEST MATCH SPECIAL, BBC radio's cricket commentary.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand displays or performances are spectacles, impressive things put on show.

clue.text: Secure area then look out protective clothing

parts.note: to pin something is to secure it
Fore! is the golfer's shout warning people to look out for a ball

explanation.surface: Instructions to fence off a zone and then keep watch, all in safety gear.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is the golf warning shouted when a ball is heading for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is an apron-like garment worn to keep clothes clean.

clue.text: Nip home without finishing place in Devon

parts.note: a nip of whisky is a tot

indicators.note: without finishing means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone popping home but never quite getting there, somewhere in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without finishing' trims NEST to NES. Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Totnes is a market town in south Devon, on the River Dart.

clue.text: Answer to 3 English chaps in temporary shelter

indicators.note: in means the letters go inside the shelter word

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter
men are chaps

explanation.surface: Englishmen camping out as a response to a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the containment signal. 'Answer to 3' means another kind of the high-rise housing defined at 3-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building of rented flats, an alternative to the tower block in clue 3.

clue.text: Look after cook

definitions.meaning: to pamper and over-protect someone is to look after them indulgently
to cook an egg gently in water just below boiling

explanation.surface: A household instruction to care for the chef.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: pampering a person, and simmering eggs gently below the boil.

clue.text: Girl coming out left overwhelmed by great disaster

parts.note: a deb, debutante, is a young woman making her society debut, 'coming out'

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the letter is engulfed inside the word for great

parts.note: ace means great, excellent

explanation.surface: A debutante's departure ending in a huge catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overwhelmed by' puts L inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden humiliating failure or collapse, a fiasco.

clue.text: Feud erupting at event interrupted by Democrat

indicators.note: interrupted by means a letter breaks into the middle of the shuffled letters
erupting suggests things flying apart, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A long-running quarrel boiling over at a political gathering when a Democrat butts in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erupting' rearranges AT EVENT to VENETTA, and 'interrupted by' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged bitter quarrel, a blood feud between families.

clue.text: One in French city on start of trip?

definitions.text: One in French city on start of trip?

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the city name

parts.note: Tours is a city on the Loire in France
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: start of means only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A visitor in a French city just setting out on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside TOURS, then 'start of' adds T. The whole clue describes a sightseer.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor travelling in a foreign city at the beginning of a holiday is a sightseer.

clue.text: In M*A*S*H, pass would be shown with this gun

indicators.note: the pass word shown alongside the gun makes the mash, so taking it away leaves the gun

parts.note: colcannon is an Irish dish of mashed potato with cabbage, a mash
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Reference to the Korean War sitcom, where a password would be backed up with a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: M*A*S*H is the TV comedy, but here it simply means mash, the potato dish colcannon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon is a large heavy gun, typically mounted on wheels.

clue.text: Supporter backed new attire for referee

indicators.note: backed means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment that supports

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan who backed a fresh kit for the match official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns BRA into ARB, and 'new' rearranges ATTIRE to ITRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To referee a dispute is to judge it between the parties, so both verbs mean settle it.

clue.text: Torture regularly fails to appear right

indicators.note: every other letter of the word vanishes on a regular beat, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A claim that torture keeps failing to produce correct results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly fails to appear' keeps the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of Torture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something correct or accurate is right, the same sense as true.

clue.text: Give birth to wild animal

definitions.meaning: to ... a child is to give birth to it
a large furry carnivore such as a grizzly

explanation.surface: A wild creature giving birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the verb for producing young, and the large animal of the forests.

clue.text: Part of a pack, returned dark-coloured clothes

indicators.note: returned means the concealed letters are read backwards
clothes is a verb here: the words cover, or clothe, the answer within them

explanation.surface: A section of a pack with its gloomy garments sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' finds KCOL within dark-coloured, and 'returned' reverses it. A lock is a rugby forward in the second row of the scrum, the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union, a lock is one of the second-row forwards in the scrum, the pack.

clue.text: Unsure and cutting about Sheeran retiring

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one word goes round another

parts.note: a cutting remark is incisive, sharp and penetrating

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the name is reversed

parts.note: Ed Sheeran, the English singer-songwriter

explanation.surface: A sharp critic wavering over a pop star's withdrawal from the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheeran is pop singer Ed Sheeran; 'retiring' reverses his first name and 'about' puts it inside the word for cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot make up their mind is irresolute, wavering and unsure.

clue.text: She made Adrian M a bit of a pudding

parts.note: Sue Townsend, the novelist, is the woman meant
she created Adrian Mole; her surname cut to its initial, T, mirrors the clue cutting Mole to M

explanation.surface: The author of Adrian Mole contributed a little to a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Sue Townsend wrote The Secret Diary of Adrian Mole; the clue writes her as Sue T, in the same clipped style as 'Adrian M'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shredded beef or mutton fat is a classic ingredient of steamed puddings and dumplings.

clue.text: Detective losing vehicle on vacation could be troublemaker

indicators.note: losing means the following letters are removed from the word for detective

parts.note: a detective is an investigator

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied of its contents, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: A sleuth whose car goes missing while away on holiday turns troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties vehicle to VE, and 'losing' takes VE from INVESTIGATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: One who incites or stirs up trouble is someone who starts it, a ringleader or agitator.
